node-1.label: Large annular erythematous plaque on lower back with centrifugal expansion and mild pruritus

node-2.label: The plaque appeared in June (1 month previously) and had centrifugally expanded; physical exam showed a 35-cm semicircular erythematous plaque on lower back with central clearing and a well-demarcated papular border.

node-3.label: Mild pruritus did not respond to conventional antihistamine therapy or topical steroids.

node-4.label: No history of arthropod bite or travel outside Spain; no relation to hobbies or skin care products.

node-5.label: 20-year history of similar annular plaques recurring on the trunk every summer and spontaneously resolving by autumn; lesions never appeared on face, hands, or feet.

why.why: The biopsy finding of superficial perivascular lymphocytic infiltration with mild papillary dermal edema and no epidermal changes is interpreted by both the pathologist and laboratory physician as consistent with the reactive inflammatory pattern of erythema annulare centrifugum. PAS negativity essentially excludes tinea. The 20-year summer-only self-limiting course and absence of systemic involvement further support this diagnosis. Confidence is raised to 0.85; however, ANA, anti-Ro/SSA, and direct immunofluorescence results remain unavailable, so cutaneous lupus cannot be entirely excluded.

PAS-negative biopsy with no fungal elements, lack of exposure history, and a 20-year summer recurrence with spontaneous autumn resolution without antifungal treatment all argue strongly against tinea corporis. Both experts interpret the histology as essentially excluding dermatophyte infection, so confidence is reduced from 0.15 to 0.05.

Histology lacks interface changes, epidermal involvement, and atypical lymphocytes, making cutaneous lupus significantly less likely. However, serum ANA, anti-Ro/SSA, and direct immunofluorescence results are missing, so cutaneous lupus cannot be completely excluded. The long seasonal self-limiting course and absence of systemic involvement also argue against an active autoimmune process. Confidence is reduced to 0.10.

Histology shows no atypical lymphocytes, and the 20-year self-limiting seasonal course without progression or systemic involvement strongly argues against cutaneous T-cell lymphoma. The laboratory physician also notes that the absence of atypical lymphoid infiltrate significantly lowers this possibility. Confidence is reduced to 0.05.

node-10.label: Skin biopsy shows superficial perivascular lymphocytic infiltrate in the superficial dermis with mild papillary dermal edema and no epidermal changes.

node-11.label: Skin biopsy PAS stain is negative for fungal elements.

node-12.label: Histology shows no interface changes, no atypical lymphocytes, and no follicular keratin plugs.

node-13.label: No systemic involvement has occurred during the 20-year recurrent seasonal course.
